subject: Trace egress & preservation options — HealthX compliance Q&A

Subject: Trace export options and retention window questions

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking this — we're kicking off a compliance review and need a clear picture of how Redwood provides audit/access traces for tenants. A few specific items from our audit team: 

- Can you provide the maximum retention window for access logs and for admin/audit trails in hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments?
- What export formats do you support for bulk handover (NDJSON, Parquet, CSV)?
- Delivery options: signed S3 URL, direct SFTP push, or on-prem agent? Any ETA SLA for bulk exports?
- For deletion requests, we need an attestation flow: how will you prove records were deleted from backups/archives?

If you have a sample manifest (field list + schema example) that would be ideal. We're trying to line this up with our legal/infosec timeline — target is to have contract language by end of month.

Thanks,
Alex

HealthX

Alex Nguyen
security+compliance@healthx.com
From: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@healthx.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Trace export options and retention window questions

Alex — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I'm attaching our current export spec as a starting point (audit-export-spec_v2.pdf). We'll tailor the details to your residency/PII needs.

- Retention windows (defaults): hosted API access logs = 90 days; hosted audit trails = 1 year (365 days). Dedicated customers can request longer retention as part of their contract (configurable up to 3 years). Private/on-prem deployments are customer-managed and can retain indefinitely per their infra policy.

- Export formats: we support NDJSON and gzipped NDJSON (preferred for streaming), Parquet slices for large bulk exports, and CSV for small slices. The manifest includes per-file schema and row counts.

- Delivery: signed S3 POST/GET with pre-signed URLs (rotated), SFTP push (enterprise option), and secure HTTPS delivery to a customer-managed endpoint. For on-prem we can provide an ephemeral export agent that writes to your internal storage. Typical export window: 24-72 hours for a standard bulk snapshot (depends on volume); SLA-backed expedited exports possible on Dedicated with an agreed lead time.

- Deletion attestation: we emit a signed export manifest that lists object checksums and a deletion token. For hosted exports we also provide an erase playbook with tombstone records and a deletion certificate after purge. For contractual guarantees we provide attestation statements and indexed manifests showing checksums pre- and post-erase.

Next steps: can you confirm the format you prefer (NDJSON v Parquet) and whether you need PII redaction/hashing in the handed-off artifacts? If you want, we can set a tech call (30m) tomorrow to walk the spec.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: audit-export-spec_v2.pdf
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-08T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Trace export options and retention window questions — technical details

Alex / team — adding the infra details you asked for. Highlights:

- Fields & schema: each trace record exports with timestamp (ISO8601), tenant_id, request_id, route, model_id, user_agent, ip_country, action, result_code, and optional user_id (if enabled). PII fields (user_id, ip) can be hashed or redacted at export time. See attached sample manifest for column ordering.

- Format notes: NDJSON is streaming-friendly and preserves event order; Parquet is columnar and much smaller for multi-GB exports. We generate file-level checksums (SHA256) and include them in manifest.csv for integrity verification.

- Transport & encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit, server-side AES-256 for pre-signed S3 uploads, and option to deliver encrypted containers (customer-provided keys or our KMS). Pre-signed URLs expire by default after 7 days; we can extend per contract.

- Deletion proof: for hosted tenants we maintain a delivery+erase audit chain. Deletion includes: 1) manifest updated with deleted object tombstones, 2) checksum mismatch check, 3) a signed deletion certificate (PKI-backed) that we provide to the customer. For Dedicated, we can provide access to the deletion job logs and a time-stamped manifest entry.

- Edge cases: for long tail retention (multi-year) we recommend Parquet cold-slices and a lifecycle policy to archive to a customer bucket. Restores are possible but will incur retrieval latency.

Attachment: log-manifest-sample.csv

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Mateo / Karthik — good level of detail. A couple of follow-ups from our legal/compliance teams: 

1) Chain-of-custody: we need to document the handoff process for evidentiary exports. Can Redwood provide a template chain-of-custody form and sign-off flow?
2) Deletion SLA: our requirement is proof of deletion from all primary and replicated stores within 30 days of request for hosted tenants — can Redwood commit to that for a paid SLA?
3) Fed-style evidence: for certain audits we may require a PKI-signed deletion certificate and export manifest hashed into an immutable log (we use an internal attestation system). Can you support providing the signed artifacts in a format we can ingest?

If those three are feasible, let's schedule a 30-minute hangout to confirm operational runbook and a tentative timeline for contract language. We're available Nov 10 at 10:00 PT.

-Rajiv
